messages:
Anya: FYI customer (enterprise) just sent a SOC2+HIPAA checklist asking for verifiable audit ingest and per-tenant visibility guarantees. They want to include this as an SLA exhibit.
Devon: can you paste the asks here? i saw the note but not the details.
Anya: copied key points from their email:
- cryptographically verifiable events (customer can independently verify)
- tie events to key identifiers (KMS/HSM) and rotation history
- proof-of-delivery for daily bundles (receipt + integrity hash)
- RBAC: event-level tenant scoping must be enforced and auditable
- schema versioning and compatibility notes for contract
- potential 7-year export requests (cost / SLA implications)
Marta: for FedRAMP-style customers, CMK (customer-managed keys) or HSM-backed signing is usually mandatory. important to be explicit if we hold signing keys vs customer holds them.
Ben: technical note: independent verification implies asymmetric signatures (RSA/ECDSA). HMACs don't let customers verify without sharing secrets.
Devon: agree. two broad options:
1) Redwood-sign: we sign events and publish public keys + rotation metadata (easy for customers to verify).
2) CMK-remote-sign: we call customer KMS (AWS KMS Sign / GCP KMS) to sign event digests on their key. we never hold private key.
Marta: option 2 strong for compliance but will require cross-account IAM bindings and a support matrix per cloud provider.
Ben: Implementation details:
- for high volume, per-event signing via external KMS adds latency. consider batching + merkle-tree per day and sign merkle root.
- per-event receipts (signed token returned at ingest) are simpler but increase per-event cost for high throughput.
Anya: proposal: default = merkle-root daily bundles signed by either Redwood key or CMK; opt-in per-tenant for per-event receipts.
Devon: example canonical event we propose to include in the bundle (deterministic ordering, compact):
```
{"event_id":"evt_20260318_0001","tenant_id":"acme-123","action":"model.generate","ts":"2026-03-18T16:12:03Z","payload_sha256":"sha256:abcd...","schema_v":"2"}
```
Signature bundle attached to daily archive should include: signer_key_id, signing_alg, canonical_v, signature, rotation_proof_url (if applicable).
Marta: schema note: add optional fields `signer_key_id` and `signature_bundle` at schema_v=2. mark them optional so old consumers not affected. add schema deprecation policy in docs.
Ben: merkle approach sketch:
- compute per-event leaf = sha256(canonical_event)
- build merkle tree for day
- sign merkle_root with chosen key
- publish merkle_root + index file and allow customers to request inclusion proof for event_id
Devon: receipt approach sketch:
- on ingest we respond with `receipt_token` that contains event_id, ingest_node, ts and is signed by Redwood/CMK
- customer stores receipt; later they compare to bundle/merkle proof
Legal: contract implications:
- define acceptance tests: Redwood will deliver sample signed bundle for tenant X; customer validates with provided verifier; 5 business days to flag discrepancies; remedies: re-issue, replay, or SLA credits per breach schedule.
- need explicit definitions: what is "delivered" (S3 link + SHA256 + signed manifest), what qualifies as late (UTC boundary + 24h), and evidence required to claim breach.
Ops: retention/export cost: estimates needed. 7-year cold archive will increase storage and retrieval cost; recommend tiered pricing + optional assisted export service.
Marta: CMK flows to investigate:
- remote-sign via AWS KMS Sign (we call customer key) — pros: non-repudiation, cons: IAM complexity, cross-region latency
- bring-your-key: customer rotates keys and we fetch public certs (no signing). but then customers would have to verify with cert chain.
Ben: rotation and verification: publish public key endpoint with key IDs, iat/exp, and rotation history. versioned manifest helps customers validate old bundles.
security-bot: [alert] low severity CVE in audit-exporter dependency. patch planned for next release; will update thread when merged.
Devon: action items (owners + due dates):
- Devon: draft canonicalization rules + signature bundle spec (due Mon EOD)
- Ben: prototype merkle daily bundle generator and inclusion proof API (due Tue)
- Marta: outline CMK remote-sign integration and IAM patterns (due Tue)
- Ops: cost model for 7-year retention + export scenarios (due Tue)
- Legal: draft SLA exhibit language + acceptance test steps (due Tue)
Anya: one more point — we need to ensure logs don't accidentally contain raw payloads if those payloads are PHI. only store payload hashes in any outward-facing index; raw payloads remain in encrypted vaults with access controls.
Ben: agreed. signature verification tools we ship should take canonical_event or the payload hash only; never log raw contents in plaintext.
Devon: can eng-platform/infra confirm adding optional `signer_key_id` + `schema_v` won't break fleet? tagging @ops @eng-platform
Ops: we'll run a compatibility suite on staging and gate tenants who opt into signed bundles. we'll also add a feature-flag per tenant for CMK flows.
Anya: thanks everyone — please drop PR links into this thread when ready. I'll consolidate a one-pager for customer success and the sales/legal packet by Wed morning. :thumbsup:
